theater: 珍珠港與西太平洋戰場

battle.name: 太平洋戰爭
battle.theater: 珍珠港與西太平洋戰場
battle.brief: 1941年12月7日清晨，日本海軍航空母艦機動部隊奇襲夏威夷珍珠港，太平洋戰爭就此開打，日軍同時在馬來西亞、緬甸、荷屬東印度與菲律賓全面進攻。卡面的1840年法軍雷管步槍並未在戰場出現，但它確立的雷管起爆原理正是當年各國步槍彈藥的共同祖型，改變的不只是射程，還有整個戰場的編組方式。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 這場戰爭是1941年12月到1945年9月的一場橫跨半個地球的全球性戰爭，日本與英美荷澳等國在亞洲、太平洋與東南亞的陸地、海洋與天空同時交鋒，交戰國多達三十餘個，戰事前後延續三年九個月。軸心國一方的核心是日本：帝國陸軍以大本營為最高統帥，1941年底至1945年先後組建南方作戦軍，轄第十一、十六、十七、十八、二十三、二十五、三十一軍等部隊，關東軍則死守滿洲；海軍以聯合艦隊為最高作戰指揮，山本五十六任總長至1943年戰死，其後由田中三成接手，1944年再由豐田副武接任，而真正的決策核心在海軍軍令部，部長永野修身與作戰參謀宇垣一成的影響往往更大。德國與義大利在珍珠港同日對美宣戰，但德軍主力留在歐洲，在太平洋只能靠潛艇與少量水面部隊騷擾。同盟國一方的核心是美國：海軍以太平洋艦隊、第三艦隊與第五艦隊承擔主要海上戰役，海軍作戰部長歐內斯特·金直接統籌；陸軍與陸戰隊在西太平洋歸麥克阿瑟的西南太平洋戰區，在中太平洋歸海軍主導的中央太平洋戰線，兩條戰線互相調配部隊與物資。英國皇家海軍以東印度艦隊與遠東艦隊承擔印度洋方向，澳洲皇家海軍、紐西蘭皇家海軍與荷蘭皇家海軍分別守住珊瑚海、紐西蘭與荷屬東印度，蘇聯直到1945年8月才由西線對日開戰，中國戰場則自1937年起與太平洋戰爭並行，英美空軍的第十四大隊長期在雲南上空作戰，直到1945年8月15日。
countriesEn: This war was a global conflict spanning half the globe, fought from December 1941 to September 1945, in which Japan fought the British, American, Dutch and Australian powers at the same time across the land, the seas and the skies of Asia, the Pacific and South-East Asia; more than thirty countries took part, and the fighting ran for three years and nine months. At the core of the Axis side was Japan: the Imperial Japanese Army took its orders from the Imperial General Headquarters, formed the Southern Expeditionary Army Group from late 1941 through 1945, and put it in charge of the Eleventh, Sixteenth, Seventeenth, Eighteenth, Twenty-third, Twenty-fifth and Thirty-first Armies, while the Kwantung Army held Manchuria; the Navy fought under the Combined Fleet, with Isoroku Yamamoto as Fleet Admiral until his death in 1943, succeeded by Sanmiichi Tanaka and then by Jozo Togo from 1944, while the real centre of decision lay in the Naval General Staff, where the influence of the Chief of the Staff Teijiro Nagano and of the operations officer Ichisei Uga was often the greater. Germany and Italy declared war on the United States on the same day as the strike on Pearl Harbor, but the bulk of the German armed forces stayed in Europe, and in the Pacific the Axis could only harass with submarines and a few surface units. At the core of the Allied side was the United States: the Navy carried the main burden of the naval war through the Pacific Fleet, the Third Fleet and the Fifth Fleet under the Chief of Naval Operations, Ernest King; the Army and the Marine Corps operated in the South-West Pacific under MacArthur's South-West Pacific Area and in the central Pacific on the Central Pacific line led by the Navy, and the two fronts drew troops and supplies from each other. The Royal Navy carried the Indian Ocean with the Eastern Fleet and the Far East Fleet, the Royal Australian Navy, the Royal New Zealand Navy and the Royal Netherlands Navy respectively held the Coral Sea, New Zealand and the Netherlands East Indies, the Soviet Union entered the war against Japan only from the west in August 1945, and the China front ran in parallel with the Pacific War from 1937 onward, with the British and American Fourteenth Air Force flying over Yunnan until 15 August 1945.
people: 這場戰爭的關鍵人物，一半在珍珠港的指揮室裡，一半在中太平洋的艦橋上。日本方面，聯合艦隊總長山本五十六統籌艦隊與基地航空隊，策劃了以空母機動打擊夏威夷的奇襲，也把中途島的戰役改為四支打擊艦隊分進合擊；策劃這套方案的海軍作戰參謀宇垣一成與參謀長武備敏功不可沒。山本把空母群與艦載機分作數個打擊大隊，而護衛驅逐艦與戰鬥艦隊之間的情報被破解，遂在1943年4月於所羅門群島上空被擊落身亡。軍令部部長永野修身是「長期打算」的推手，1941年12月的御前會議由他與陸軍參謀長杉山元分別代表軍令部與陸軍作最後陳述；陸軍方面，1941年11月5日的御前會議由近衛文麿主持並裁定南進，山下奉文的第二十五軍三周之內打穿英軍在馬來西亞的防線，齋藤義次的第二十三軍攻入仰光；1944年美軍登陸呂宋之後，主持南方作戰的安藤利一與牟田口廉也相繼被解職。盟軍方面，尼米茲以情報與工業實力主導中太平洋的消耗戰，麥克阿瑟以蛙跳戰術在西南太平洋逐島推進，弗萊徹、哈爾西、斯普魯恩斯與特納在海上的決策改變了整場戰爭；佩西瓦爾在新加坡的投降、萬達格里夫特在瓜島的固守與溫賴特在科雷吉多的堅持，都成為雙方記述之中最常被引用的段落。
peopleEn: The key figures of this war were half of them in a command room at Pearl Harbor and half of them on the bridges of carriers in the central Pacific. On the Japanese side, Fleet Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto commanded the Combined Fleet and the land-based air forces, planned the carrier strike against Hawaii, and also reshaped the battle of Midway into four strike groups converging from separate directions; the operations officer Ichisei Uga and the Combined Fleet chief of staff Takeshi Takagi were indispensable in drawing up that plan. Yamamoto split the carrier force and the air group into several strike divisions, and once the intelligence between the screening destroyers and the battle line was broken, he was shot down over the Solomon Islands in April 1943. Chief of the Naval General Staff Teijiro Nagano was the advocate of the long-term plan, and at the imperial conference of December 1941 he and the Army Chief of Staff Hajime Sugiyama made the final presentations on behalf of the General Staff and the Army respectively; on the Army side, the imperial conference of 5 November 1941 was presided over by Fumimaro Konoe, who ruled for the southern advance, Tomoyuki Yamashita's Twenty-fifth Army broke the British line in Malaya within three weeks, and Yoshitsugu Saito's Twenty-third Army drove into Rangoon; after the American landings on Luzon in 1944, Rikichi Ando, who commanded the southern operations, and Ryoya Muta-guchi were relieved of their commands in turn. On the Allied side, Nimitz ran the war of attrition in the central Pacific on the strength of intelligence and industrial output, MacArthur advanced island by island across the south-west Pacific by the technique of leapfrogging, and the decisions made afloat by Fletcher, Halsey, Spruance and Turner changed the course of the entire war; the surrender of Percival at Singapore, the stubborn defence of Guadalcanal by Vandegrift and the resistance of Wainwright at Corregidor are among the passages most often quoted in the records on both sides.
kits: 卡面這件雷管步槍是1840年前後的法制單發膛線步槍，槍身仍是木製，擊發機制用雷管撞擊底火，取代了舊式的火繩與火燧。它不會出現在1941年的戰場上，但它確立的原理卻是那場戰爭所有步槍的共同祖先：從雷管起爆的思路一路推下去，歐洲在十九世紀下半葉換裝後膛裝藥，彈藥由瓶裝火藥改為金屬彈殼加底火，到1941年全世界步兵手上的步槍幾乎都靠底火點火。日本陸軍主力是三十六年式（後改九八式）步槍，六五公厘，栓動，雙排五發；美國陸軍是M1加蘭德步槍，七六二公厘，導氣式，橋夾八發，1941年才大量配發；德國是Karabiner 98k；英國是李-恩菲爾德四型；蘇聯是莫辛-拿甘特九一／三〇式；法國是MAS一五式。支撐武器方面，各國普遍裝備機槍：美軍有勃朗寧M1919輕機槍、M1918步槍與M2重機槍，德軍有MG34與MG42，英軍有布侖與維克斯，蘇軍有DP-27，日軍則以九二式重機槍與九六式、九九式輕機槍支撐。迫擊砲以美軍六〇與八一公厘最常見，日軍用九七式九〇公厘迫擊砲，英軍有二吋與三吋迫擊砲。裝甲方面有M3李-Grant、M4雪曼、M5斯圖爾特與日軍九五式輕型坦克、九七式坦克。航空與海戰方面，日軍以零式戰鬥機、偵察機與艦上轟炸機為核心，美軍有SB2C無畏艦式艦載俯衝轟炸機、TBF雷神艦載魚雷機、P-38閃電、F4U野蠻式戰鬥機與B-24、B-29轟炸機，雙方都有潛水艦、魚雷艇與姊妹艦。除了武器，後勤器材同樣決定勝負：日本在馬來西亞戰役中徵用自行車近十萬輛，荷屬東印度軍有軍馬約八千匹，澳洲輕騎兵與蘇蒙騎兵在紐幾里亞及滿洲多只擔任偵察與警戒。
kitsEn: The piece on the card is a French single-shot muzzle-loading percussion rifle of about 1840: the stock is still wooden, and the firing mechanism uses a percussion cap struck against a priming compound, replacing the older matchlock and flintlock. It would not be found on any battlefield in 1941, but the principle it established was the common ancestor of every service rifle in that war: following the idea of igniting the charge by percussion, Europe went over to breech-loading in the second half of the nineteenth century, cartridges changed from loose powder in bottles to metal cases with a primer in the base, and by 1941 almost every infantryman in the world fired a round that went off because of a primer. The Japanese Army's standard was the Type 38 (later the Type 99) rifle in 6.5 mm, bolt-action, five rounds; the US Army used the M1 Garand in 7.62 mm, gas-operated, eight rounds in a clip, only widely issued in 1941; Germany used the Karabiner 98k, Britain the Lee-Enfield No. 4, the Soviet Union the Mosin-Nagant 91/30, France the MAS 1915. For support weapons, machine guns were universal: the Americans had the Browning M1919 light machine gun, the M1918 BAR and the M2 heavy machine gun, the Germans the MG 34 and MG 42, the British the Bren and the Vickers, the Soviets the DP-27, and the Japanese the Type 92 heavy machine gun together with the Type 96 and Type 99 light machine guns. The commonest mortars were the US 60 mm and 81 mm, the Japanese used the Type 97 90 mm mortar and the British the 2-inch and 3-inch. In armour there were the M3 Lee/Grant, the M4 Sherman and the M5 Stuart on the Allied side, and the Japanese Type 95 light tank and Type 97 tank. In the air and at sea the Japanese centred on the Zero fighter, the reconnaissance aircraft and the carrier bombers, while the Americans had the SB2C Dauntless carrier dive-bomber, the TBF Avenger torpedo bomber, the P-38 Lightning, the F4U Corsair and the B-24 and B-29 bombers; both sides also fielded submarines, motor torpedo boats and destroyer squadrons. Beyond the weapons themselves the materiel of logistics decided the contest: Japan mobilised close to one hundred thousand bicycles for the Malayan campaign, the Royal Netherlands East Indies Army had about eight thousand horses, and the Australian light horse and the Soviet-Mongolian cavalry served in New Guinea and Manchuria mostly as reconnaissance and security troops.
tactics: 珍珠港的奇襲是一套完整計算過的操作：艦隊11月26日從佐世保出發，取北道以避開巡邏，穿越北太平洋的風浪，在距夏威夷約一千九百公里的位置放出第一個攻擊大隊，六個攻擊大隊分波次俯衝轟炸，第一波在珍珠港上空投彈，第二波補炸，隨後飛鷹與蒼龍的魚雷機低空突入，攻擊港內的戰列艦；當時珍珠港雷達的天線未架設成功，艦隊又停在雲層與逆光之下，警戒的哨兵因戰前的爆炸聲誤判為本土空襲。海上作戰的骨幹是「航空母艦打擊群」，把艦載機分成數個打擊大隊，先以半數兵力在敵方海域遊蕩分散注意，再由主力大隊自側翼突入，俯衝轟炸與魚雷攻擊反覆施加在沒有護衛的運輸船隊上。1941年12月的馬來亞，日軍以縱隊沿西海岸公路推進，用自行車部隊與步兵混合的縱隊突破英軍的縱深防禦；反過來在緬甸，仰光等口岸的失守逼英軍放棄了固守。島嶼攻略的核心是蛙跳與前進基地：美軍以帕勞、關島、塞班、提尼安排成一串基地，飛行半徑控制在六百海里以內，陸戰隊在硫黃島與沖繩以艦炮與航空兵支援登陸，而日軍則靠洞窟、坑道與縱深梯地反擊。瓜達爾卡納爾是典型的消耗戰：海軍陸戰隊守住了灘頭與機場，日軍以「東京」高速貨輪送補，六個月裡雙方傷亡數以萬計。西南太平洋的關鍵是航空與後勤的連鎖：澳洲基地的B-24與C-54把補給線從布里斯班拉到萊伊島，全線超過三千公里，空中補給與港口卸載能力決定了地面部隊能推進多快。
tacticsEn: The attack on Pearl Harbor was an operation worked out to the last detail: the force sailed from Yokosuka on 26 November, took the northern route to stay clear of patrols, crossed the heavy seas of the North Pacific, and at a point some 1,900 kilometres from Hawaii launched the first strike group, six attack divisions going in in waves of dive-bombing, the first wave dropping bombs over the harbour, the second following up, and then the torpedo aircraft of Hiryu and Soryu coming in low against the battleships in the anchorage. The radar antenna at Pearl Harbor had not been brought into operation, the fleet was lying under cloud and in the glare of the rising sun, and the lookouts, deafened by an explosion during a live-fire practice ashore, reported the attack as a raid on the mainland. The backbone of the fighting at sea was the carrier strike group: the air group was divided into several strike divisions, half the strength being sent to cruise in the enemy's waters and divide attention, and the main body then coming in from the flank, with dive-bombing and torpedo attacks repeated against convoys that had no escort. In Malaya in December 1941 the Japanese advanced in column along the west coast road, and a column of bicycles mixed with infantry broke through the British defence in depth; in Burma the other way round, the fall of Rangoon and other ports drove the British to give up fixed positions. The core of the island campaigns was leapfrogging and the chain of forward bases: the Americans strung out Palawan, Guam, Saipan and Tinian as a line of bases, kept the flying radius inside six hundred miles, and landed on Iwo Jima and Okinawa with naval gunfire and carrier aircraft in support, while the Japanese answered from caves, tunnels and terraces held in depth. Guadalcanal was a typical war of attrition: the Marines held the beachhead and the airfield, the Japanese ran supplies in with the high-speed cargo ship Tokyo, and both sides counted casualties in the tens of thousands over six months. The key in the south-west Pacific was the chain of air power and logistics: B-24s and C-54s flying from Australian bases drew the supply line from Brisbane to Leyte Island, more than three thousand kilometres in length, and the capacity of air supply and of harbour discharge decided how fast the ground forces could advance.
data: 可以給出數字的幾項：珍珠港一役，美軍陣亡二千四百零三人、受傷一千一百七十八人，四艘主力戰列艦沉沒、四艘重傷，軍機損失一百八十九架，另有約二百架在地面被摧毀；日軍出動約三百五十架次，投放炸彈與魚雷共三百五十餘枚。珊瑚海海戰是第一次航母對決，翔鶴號重傷、沈陽號被擊沉，載機母雙方互有損失。中途島海戰在1942年6月4日一日之內決定，日本損失赤城、加賀、飛鷹、雲龍四艘母艦與約二千八百名艦員、兩百餘架戰機，美軍損失一艘母艦與一艘驅逐艦，母艦上有名的飛行員陣亡率極高。瓜達爾卡納爾打了六個月，日軍陣亡約一萬九千人，美軍陣亡約一千六百人。馬里亞納海空戰中，1944年6月日本海航損失四百二十五架、美軍損失二十四架，7月是六百四十五架對六十架。硫黃島美軍陣亡六千八百二十一人，日軍守軍約二萬一千人中約一萬八千人陣亡，被俘者僅數百人。沖繩美軍陣亡約一萬二千五百人、受傷三萬八千餘人，日軍約四萬五千人參戰、陣亡約一萬人。大和號在1945年4月7日被擊沉，三千零六十三名乘員中生還者不足三百人。物資方面，1940年荷屬東印度年產原油約八百萬噸，其中婆羅洲約四百八十萬噸；日本年需石油約五百萬噸而自產不足五十萬噸，美英荷凍結日方資產之後，日本的石油進口幾乎斷絕。全戰爭中日本陸海軍及隨軍人員的死亡人數，日本官方統計在一百九十萬至二百五十萬之間，各家數字相差頗大。
dataEn: A few of the figures that can be given are these: in the attack on Pearl Harbor the Americans lost 2,403 dead and 1,178 wounded, four battleships were sunk and four more heavily damaged, 189 aircraft were lost in the air and about two hundred more were destroyed on the ground; the Japanese flew roughly 350 sorties and dropped a total of some 350 bombs and torpedoes. The Battle of the Coral Sea was the first meeting of carrier forces, the Shokaku was badly damaged, the Shōyō was sunk, and each side lost carriers. The Battle of Midway was decided within a single day on 4 June 1942: Japan lost the carriers Akagi, Kaga, Hiryu and Shōryū, about 2,800 of their crew and more than two hundred aircraft, while the United States lost one carrier and one destroyer, the air group of the lost carrier suffering an exceptionally high rate of loss among its famous fliers. Guadalcanal ran for six months, with about 19,000 Japanese dead and about 1,600 American dead. In the air battles over the Marianas in June 1944 the Japanese lost 425 aircraft and the Americans 24, and in July the figures were 645 against 60. On Iwo Jima 6,821 Americans were killed, and of roughly 21,000 Japanese defenders about 18,000 died with only a few hundred captured. On Okinawa about 12,500 Americans were killed and more than 38,000 wounded, while of some 45,000 Japanese troops committed about 10,000 were killed. The Yamato was sunk on 7 April 1945 with fewer than three hundred survivors out of 3,063 men aboard. On materiel: in 1940 the Netherlands East Indies produced about 8,000,000 tonnes of crude oil a year, of which roughly 4,800,000 tonnes came from Borneo; Japan needed some 5,000,000 tonnes of oil a year and produced less than 500,000, and after the Anglo-American and Dutch freezing of Japanese assets the oil imports of Japan were almost cut off altogether. For the whole war the official Japanese count of dead among the army, navy and attached personnel runs from about 1.9 to 2.5 million, and the figures given by different authorities vary a good deal.
cause: 太平洋戰爭的起因是一個經濟困局與一份時間表。日本在1936年的國策基準裡就把自己定位成一個資源自給的東亞大國，但它的工業需要大量進口石油、鐵礦石與橡膠，國內年產石油不足五十萬噸而年需約五百萬噸，絕大部分靠美國供應。1940年9月日德意三國同盟條約簽訂，1940年11月13日御前會議決定南進，1940至1941年間日本佔領法屬印度支那、緬甸與泰國，1941年7月美國凍結日本在美資產並實施石油禁運，8月英荷跟進，戰爭物資的來源被切斷大半。佔領荷屬東印度可以拿回婆羅洲的油田與印尼的橡膠，佔領緬甸與馬來西亞可以拿回橡膠與錫——這就是「南方資源圈」的算盤。11月26日日本駐美大使來棲三郎向美國國務卿赫爾提交備忘錄，要求中國與印度支那的日軍撤退，與此同時珍珠港的艦隊已經在北太平洋的風浪裡行進。推動最後決策的是軍部與少壯派軍人：中國戰場陷入僵局、關東軍在滿洲無戰可打、國際地位被南方資源所困，而蘇德戰爭又把歐洲和美國的注意力拉開，正是「現在不打就永遠沒有機會」的時候。1941年12月1日御前會議決定對美開戰，12月2日海軍軍令部與陸軍參謀部分別作最後陳述，計劃的核心是：用奇襲摧毀美國太平洋艦隊，換取六到十二個月的石油，再用這段時間拿下南方資源區。
causeEn: The cause of the Pacific War was an economic trap and a timetable. Already in its national policy basis of 1936 Japan had defined itself as a self-sufficient great power of East Asia, yet its industry needed large imports of oil, iron ore and rubber, and while its own production of oil was under 500,000 tonnes a year against a need of some 5,000,000, the greater part of the supply came from the United States. The Tripartite Pact between Japan, Germany and Italy was signed in September 1940, the imperial conference decided on the southern advance on 13 November 1940, and between 1940 and 1941 Japan seized French Indochina, Burma and Thailand; in July 1941 the United States froze Japanese assets in America and imposed the oil embargo, with Britain and the Netherlands following in August, and the greater part of Japan's source of war materiel was cut off. Taking the Netherlands East Indies would bring back the oil of Borneo and the rubber of Indonesia, and taking Burma and Malaya would bring back rubber and tin: that was the arithmetic of the southern resource sphere. On 26 November the Japanese ambassador in Washington, Saburo Kurusu, delivered a note to the American Secretary of State Hull demanding the withdrawal of Japanese troops from China and Indochina, and at the same moment the Pearl Harbor force was already steaming through the North Pacific. What pushed the final decision was the General Staff and the young officers: the China front had bogged down, the Kwantung Army had no war to fight in Manchuria, the country's international position was strangled by the problem of resources, and the German-Soviet war had drawn the attention of Europe and of America elsewhere, which made it exactly the moment when there would never be a better one to fight. The imperial conference of 1 December 1941 decided on war with the United States, and on 2 December the Naval General Staff and the Army Chief of Staff made their final presentations; the core of the plan was to destroy the American Pacific Fleet by surprise, buy six to twelve months of oil, and use that time to seize the southern resource areas.
impact: 太平洋戰爭的結果，是亞洲與太平洋的整個地緣秩序被重排。歐洲殖民帝國在亞洲的統治幾乎在四年內崩塌：英屬馬來亞、荷屬與法屬印度支那在戰爭中連續斷裂，1945年8月17日蘇加諾宣讀印度尼西亞獨立宣言，9月2日胡志明宣布越南獨立，1947年印度與巴基斯坦獨立，1951年緬甸與寮國分別取得自治與獨立。台灣與澎湖在1945年10月25日回歸中國，朝鮮在戰後依美蘇以北緯三十八度分界，北方由蘇聯占領，南方由美國占領。美國從此成為太平洋的支配者：在夏威夷、關島、塞班、提尼安與橫濱建立起一整圈基地，海軍從一個大西洋國家變成兩大洋國家，1947年援助歐洲的馬歇爾計劃則把它推向世界霸主的位置。蘇聯以八月初的參戰換得旅順、大連的租借權、中蘇合資的南滿鐵路與千島群島的實際控制，成為戰後東亞格局的關鍵一子。日本則被徹底改造：1945年11月的幣制改革、財閥解散、1946年制憲時第九條把戰爭能力寫成永久禁止，1951年舊金山和約與1952年對美安保條約把日本綁進西方陣營，1956年日蘇共同宣言處理北方四島，戰後的日本靠出口與美國市場重新站起來，成為亞洲四小龍之中最早的一個。中國在這場戰爭中取得聯合國安理會常任理事國的席位，卻在勝利之後立刻陷入全面內戰。原子彈在1945年8月6日與9日落在廣島與長崎，人類自此面對可以一次抹平一座城市的武器；聯合國在同年10月生效，世界從歐洲戰爭的落幕直接滑進冷戰的開端。
impactEn: The result of the Pacific War was that the whole geopolitical order of Asia and the Pacific was rearranged. The rule of the European colonial powers in Asia collapsed within four years: British Malaya and the Dutch and French possessions in Indochina were cut off one after another, Sukarno proclaimed Indonesian independence on 17 August 1945, Ho Chi Minh proclaimed the independence of Vietnam on 2 September, India and Pakistan became independent in 1947, and Burma and Laos gained autonomy and independence in 1951. Taiwan and the Pescadores returned to China on 25 October 1945, and Korea was divided after the war along the thirty-eighth parallel between the Soviet and the American zones, the north falling to Soviet occupation and the south to American. From then on the United States was the master of the Pacific: a whole ring of bases at Hawaii, Guam, Saipan, Tinian and Yokohama turned a navy of an Atlantic power into a navy of two oceans, and the Marshall Plan of 1947, which assisted Europe, pushed the country on to the position of world hegemon. The Soviet Union paid for its entry into the war in early August with the lease of Port Arthur and Dalian, with joint Sino-Soviet ownership of the South Manchurian Railway and with effective control of the Kuril Islands, and became a decisive piece in the post-war order of East Asia. Japan, for its part, was remade from the ground up: the currency reform of November 1945, the dissolution of the zaibatsu, and the Ninth Article of the 1946 constitution permanently forbidding the means of war, followed by the San Francisco Peace Treaty of 1951 and the US-Japan Security Treaty of 1952 tying Japan into the Western camp and the 1956 Japan-Soviet Joint Declaration dealing with the northern islands; the Japan of the post-war years stood up again on exports and the American market and became the earliest of the four Asian tigers. China gained a permanent seat on the Security Council of the United Nations out of this war, and fell immediately into a civil war on every front now that the war was over. The atomic bombs fell on Hiroshima and Nagasaki on 6 and 9 August 1945, and from that day humanity confronted a weapon able to erase a city in a single blow; the United Nations came into force in October of the same year, and the world slid straight from the ending of the war in Europe into the opening of the Cold War.
result: 結果是日本帝國在亞洲與太平洋的體系全面崩解。1945年8月8日蘇聯宣戰，8月9日凌晨對滿洲、北方四島與庫頁島的進攻展開，蒙古人民共和國同時出兵，關東軍約七十五萬人被牽制在北方的戰線上，無法南下救援；8月10日關東軍提出停戰，8月15日正午日本天皇以詔書宣布接受波茨坦宣言，9月2日上午九時十一分日本代表在密蘇里號戰艦的甲板上簽署投降書，戰爭自9月3日起正式結束。整場戰爭的勝負其實在1942年6月就大致定了：中途島之後日本喪失主動攻擊能力，1943年底到1944年上半年的馬里亞納與萊城-萊伊戰役裡，日本的航空母艦、運輸船與海軍航空兵被系統性地消滅，1945年4月大和號的沉沒只是這條曲線的最後一段。戰術層面上，珍珠港是歷史上最完整的奇襲作業，戰略層面上卻是一場破產，山本五十六自己說聯合艦隊贏了一場大勝，卻站在了山頂上沒有路可下；瓜達爾卡納爾與新幾里亞的叢林消耗戰把雙方的後勤與士氣磨到見底；蛙跳戰術與前進基地網把孤立的前哨一個個拔掉，每推進一千公里就要重新建立一套港口、機場與倉庫體系；而決定性的武器不是大炮，是能連續生產、能可靠發射、能由後勤持續補上的步槍、艦載機與運輸船。
resultEn: The outcome was the complete collapse of the Japanese Empire's system in Asia and the Pacific. The Soviet Union declared war on 8 August 1945, and at dawn on 9 August the invasion of Manchuria, the northern islands and Sakhalin opened, with the Mongolian People's Republic entering the war at the same time; some 750,000 men of the Kwantung Army were pinned on the northern front and could not be sent south to help. The Kwantung Army asked for an armistice on 10 August, and at noon on 15 August the Emperor of Japan broadcast a rescript accepting the Potsdam Declaration; at 9:11 in the morning on 2 September the Japanese representatives signed the instrument of surrender on the deck of the battleship Missouri in Tokyo Bay, and the war formally ended on 3 September. The verdict of the whole war was in fact settled in substance in June 1942: after Midway Japan lost the capacity to strike on the initiative, and in the Marianas and in the Leyte-Leyte campaign from late 1943 to the first half of 1944 the Japanese carriers, transports and naval air force were systematically destroyed, and the sinking of the Yamato in April 1945 was only the last stretch of that curve. On the tactical level Pearl Harbor was the most complete surprise operation in history; on the strategic level it was a bankruptcy, as Yamamoto said himself, that the Combined Fleet had won a great victory and found itself at the top of a mountain with no way down. The jungle war of attrition at Guadalcanal and in New Guinea wore both sides' logistics and morale down to the bone; the leapfrog technique and the chain of forward bases pulled out one isolated outpost after another, and every thousand kilometres of advance meant building a fresh set of harbours, airfields and warehouses. And the decisive weapon was never the big gun: it was the rifle, the carrier aircraft and the transport ship, things that could be produced in series, fired reliably, and kept supplied by the logistics.
